headword: {球根|きゅうこん}{植物|しょくぶつ}
reading: きゅうこんしょくぶつ

definitions.explanation: A plant that grows from an underground bulb and overwinters as the bulb stores nutrients. Typical examples include tulips, lilies, and daffodils.

examples.japanese: チューリップは{球根|きゅうこん}{植物|しょくぶつ}だ。
{秋|あき}に{球根|きゅうこん}{植物|しょくぶつ}の{球根|きゅうこん}を{植|う}えると、{春|はる}に{花|はな}が{咲|さ}く。
examples.english: If you plant the bulbs of bulb plants in autumn, they will bloom in spring.

examples.japanese: {球根|きゅうこん}{植物|しょくぶつ}は、{地上部|ちじょうぶ}が{枯|か}れても{地中|ちちゅう}の{球根|きゅうこん}で{栄養|えいよう}を{蓄|たくわ}える。
examples.english: Even when the above-ground parts wither, bulb plants store nutrients in the bulb underground.

notes:
Compound of {球根|きゅうこん} (bulb) and {植物|しょくぶつ} (plant). A horticultural category covering plants that survive unfavorable seasons by storing nutrients in an underground bulb. Commonly encountered in gardening magazines, flower shops, and school science classes.

COMMON EXAMPLES:
- チューリップ: tulip
- ユリ: lily
- スイセン: daffodil
- ヒヤシンス: hyacinth
- スノードロップ: snowdrop

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {球根|きゅうこん}{植物|しょくぶつ}を{育|そだ}てる: to grow bulb plants
- {球根|きゅうこん}{植物|しょくぶつ}の{球根|きゅうこん}を{植|う}える: to plant the bulbs of bulb plants

RELATED WORDS:
- {球根|きゅうこん}: bulb — the storage organ itself
- {多年草|たねんそう}: perennial plant — a broader category; most bulb plants are perennials
- {宿根草|しゅっこんそう}: plant that dies back above ground but resprouts from the roots — contrasted with bulb plants by its storage strategy
